subject: Acero Health field trial: success journey, owners, risks & next steps
messages:
From: Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <pshah@acerohealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-12T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Recap & proposed success metrics for the Acero field trial

Hi Priya — great call earlier. Quick recap and a proposed skinny plan to get the field trial moving. I captured the things we agreed on and a recommended cadence so your team can review before we lock dates.

Summary of ask (from Acero):
- Evaluate Redwood inference performance on clinical-document summarization pipeline (latency, summary quality, cost per call).
- Zero-PHI test data initially; targeted move to de-identified clinical notes later in trial.

Proposed success metrics (we can refine):
- Latency: 95th percentile < 350ms for 512-token requests under your representative workload.
- Quality: ROUGE-L / human-annotated accept rate >= 85% on a 50-sample holdout set.
- Cost: inference unit cost target <= $0.006/token (post-batching config).
- Stability: 99.5% request success rate during scheduled business hours.

Suggested trial structure (4 weeks):
- Week 0 (kickoff): environment access, sample dataset, runbook & evaluation template delivered.
- Week 1: baseline runs, initial tuning (batching/quantization), weekly sync.
- Week 2: guardrail checks, prefix caching enabled, quality evaluation on 50 samples.
- Week 3: ramp to scaled throughput, run acceptance tests, prepare final readout.
- Final readout: shared drive deliverables + 45-minute readout w/ execs.

Ownership I propose:
- Redwood PM (me): overall trial orchestration, weekly readout, HubSpot updates.
- Redwood CS (Marissa Cole): onboarding, runbook ops, acceptance tests.
- Redwood SE (Jonas Weber): infra configuration, instance sizing, latency tuning.
- Acero PO (Priya): success criteria signoff, access to sample dataset, procurement contacts.

Immediate next steps:
1) Priya: confirm the proposed metrics and whether a 4-week window looks right for Acero (reply by EOD Wed).
2) We will drop the trial playbook and a MUP (mutual action plan) into the shared Drive; Marissa to set environment checklist.
3) Book a 30-min kickoff during the week of Dec 20 — please share windows.

Attachments: MUP (draft) is attached for quick review — it contains milestone dates and owner rows.

Thanks — excited to get this running.

Best,
Chloe Martin
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: MUP-Acero-Success-Metrics.xlsx]

From: Priya Shah <pshah@acerohealth.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.com>
Cc: Acero Health Service Ops <service_ops@acerohealth.com>
Date: 2026-12-12T10:07:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Recap & proposed success metrics for the Acero field trial

Thanks for the thorough recap, Chloe — that aligns well with what we discussed. A few notes and a couple of asks from procurement/security before we kick off: 

Notes:
- The 4-week cadence looks reasonable; prefer kickoff during week of Dec 20 as proposed.
- Quality target: we'll run the 50-sample human review internally; can confirm pass threshold after week 1.

Security/Procurement asks: 
1) Can you attach the SOC2 evidence (summary) and your standard DPA? Our InfoSec requires a short checklist to review before we process a POC SOW.
2) Data residency: for the de-identified set we plan to share in Week 2, it must remain in the US region and not persist beyond the trial retention window (30 days). Please confirm retention/erasure controls.

I'll loop in procurement if the DPA and SOC2 summary are provided. Also, could Redwood confirm whether the trial environment will support prefix/KV caching (we expect to test that)?

I'll aim to confirm metrics/signoff by Dec 15.

—Priya
Director of Product, Acero Health
pshah@acerohealth.com
[External]

From: Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <pshah@acerohealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-12T11:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Recap & proposed success metrics for the Acero field trial

Priya — thanks. Quick answers and actions below.

Security/procurement:
- Attached: short SOC2 summary + our DPA excerpt focused on POC usage. Both are also in the shared Drive link below.
- Retention: we will provision a US-only test cluster (IAD region) and set trial retention to 30 days; after the test window runs we will run a documented erasure process and share the erasure confirmation. Jonas will own that run and provide a timestamped log.

Technical capabilities:
- Yes — prefix/KV caching is supported and we will enable a caching policy for the trial traffic; we will document how the cache interacts with batching and quantization in the runbook.

Confirmed owners & timeline (updated from the MUP):
- Kickoff: Tue Dec 21, 2026 (proposed) — 30 min. Action: everyone reply with availability; Marissa will send the invite.
- Deliverables before kickoff: 1) access form for sandbox cluster (Marissa), 2) sample data spec (Priya).
- Week 1 owner: Baseline runs & perf snapshot (Jonas).
- Week 2 owner: Quality eval and human review (Acero + Marissa).
- Week 3 owner: Scale test & final readout prep (Chloe).

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Delays from procurement on DPA/SOW -> Mitigation: Start sandbox access while DPA is in parallel; limited data set (zero-PHI) for initial runs.
- Risk: Unexpected latency spikes during scale -> Mitigation: SE-led tuning session + fallback to smaller instance types for readout.

Links: 1) HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/3245  2) Shared Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AceroTrial

Attachments: MUP updated; SOC2 summary attached as PDF.

Next steps (action owners):
- Marissa: send kickoff invite and checklist (today).
- Jonas: prepare sandbox instance spec and retention/erasure plan (by Dec 16).
- Priya: share sample data spec and confirm DPA/procurement timeline (by Dec 15).

I'll book the kickoff once I have the availability.

Best,
Chloe
[Attachments: MUP-Acero-Success-Metrics.xlsx, Acero_Security_Questionnaire.pdf]

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Priya Shah <pshah@acerohealth.com>
Date: 2026-12-12T13:42:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Recap & proposed success metrics for the Acero field trial

On 12/12/2026 11:20 AM, Chloe Martin wrote:
> Retention: we will provision a US-only test cluster (IAD region) and set trial retention to 30 days; after the test window runs we will run a documented erasure process and share the erasure confirmation.

Thanks — quick technical checklist from my side so folks know what I will deliver before kickoff:
- Sandbox spec (instance types, GPU count, network egress estimate) — will post to Drive by Dec 16.
- Data ingestion stub: S3 presigned URLs and ingestion script; request: please provide a 1–2GB zero-PHI sample or smaller subset for baseline tests.
- KV/prefix cache policy doc: how we enable/disable and metrics to watch.
- Erasure log template: will provide the format and the expected fields we will populate post-trial.

Question for Acero: what retention policy do you need on your side for retention logs (audit trail)? We typically keep audit logs for 90 days by default but can shorten on request for trial-only projects.

I'll start the sandbox spin-up once Marissa clears the access form.

—Jonas
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: infra-checklist.txt]
